question: What is the minimum tread depth required in every major groove on the front tires of a commercial motor vehicle?
explanation: The manual requires at least 4/32-inch tread depth in every major groove on front tires, and 2/32 inch on other tires.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-1

question: Re-grooved, recapped, or retreaded tires are prohibited on:
choice_a: The rear axle of a straight truck
choice_b: The front wheels of a bus
choice_d: The steer axle of an empty tractor
explanation: The manual states that re-grooved, recapped, or retreaded tires on the front wheels of a bus are prohibited.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-1

question: Excessive steering wheel play, defined as more than 10 degrees of movement (about 2 inches at the rim of a 20-inch wheel), can:
choice_c: Be ignored if the vehicle is empty
explanation: Steering wheel play of more than 10 degrees can make it hard to steer and is a defect to check for during inspection.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-2

question: During a vehicle inspection, if one-fourth or more of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing, what is the result?
choice_a: The vehicle is placed out of service
choice_b: It is only noted for the next scheduled maintenance
choice_c: It is acceptable if the load is light
choice_d: The driver must reduce speed by half
explanation: Missing or broken leaves in any leaf spring will put the vehicle 'out of service' if one-fourth or more are missing, though any defect could be dangerous.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-2

question: As part of required emergency equipment, a commercial vehicle must carry warning devices for parked vehicles, such as:
choice_b: Three reflective warning triangles, 6 fusees, or 3 liquid burning flares
explanation: Vehicles must carry warning devices for parked vehicles, such as three reflective warning triangles, 6 fusees, or 3 liquid burning flares, along with a fire extinguisher and spare fuses.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-3

question: To test a hydraulic brake system for leaks during a vehicle inspection, you should pump the brake pedal three times, then apply firm pressure and hold it for how long?
explanation: For hydraulic brakes, pump the pedal three times, then apply firm pressure and hold for five seconds. The pedal should not move; if it does, there may be a leak.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-7

question: Drivers of trucks and truck tractors transporting cargo must inspect the cargo securement within the first 50 miles of a trip, and after that, at least every:
choice_a: 50 miles or 1 hour, whichever comes first
choice_b: 150 miles or 3 hours, whichever comes first
choice_c: 250 miles or 4 hours, whichever comes first
choice_d: 500 miles or 8 hours, whichever comes first
explanation: Drivers must inspect cargo securement within the first 50 miles of a trip and every 150 miles or every three hours (whichever comes first) after that.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-7

question: When backing a commercial vehicle, why should you back and turn toward the driver's side whenever possible?
choice_a: It is required by all state laws
choice_b: You can see better by looking out the side window
choice_d: It is faster than backing to the right
explanation: Backing toward the driver's side lets you watch the rear of your vehicle by looking out the side window; backing toward the right side is dangerous because you can't see as well.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-8

question: When steering a commercial vehicle, you should hold the steering wheel:
choice_a: With one hand at the top of the wheel
choice_b: Firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel
choice_c: Loosely to allow for quick adjustments
choice_d: With both hands at the bottom of the wheel
explanation: You should hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides so it does not get pulled from your hands if you hit a curb or pothole.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-8

question: You should downshift to a lower gear in which of the following situations?
choice_a: Only when merging onto a highway
choice_b: Before starting down a hill and before entering a curve
choice_c: Only after the vehicle has already slowed down
choice_d: Only when the engine is at idle
explanation: Special conditions where you should downshift include before starting down a hill and before entering a curve, so you can control your speed without relying only on the brakes.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-9

question: You should turn off a vehicle's retarder whenever the road is:
explanation: When drive wheels have poor traction, a retarder may cause them to skid, so you should turn the retarder off whenever the road is wet, icy, or snow covered.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-10

question: Most good drivers look ahead a distance they will travel in about how many seconds?
explanation: Most good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead, which at highway speeds is about a quarter mile.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-10

question: When should you check and adjust your mirrors for accuracy?
choice_a: Only after the trip is finished
choice_b: Prior to the start of a trip, when the trailer(s) are straight
choice_d: Mirrors do not need adjusting once set
explanation: Mirror adjustment should be checked prior to the start of any trip and can only be checked accurately when the trailer(s) are straight.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-10

question: Which of the following is one of the three rules for using turn signals correctly?
choice_a: Signal only after you begin turning
choice_b: Signal early, signal continuously, and cancel your signal after the turn
choice_c: Only signal when other vehicles are visible
choice_d: Use turn signals only at night
explanation: The three rules for turn signals are: signal early, signal continuously through the turn, and cancel the signal once the turn is complete.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-10

question: If you must stop on a road or shoulder, within how many minutes must you put out your emergency warning devices?
explanation: If you must stop on a road or the shoulder of any road, you must put out your emergency warning devices within ten minutes.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-11

question: If you stop on a one-way or divided highway, where should you place your warning triangles?
choice_a: All three within 10 feet of the vehicle
choice_b: 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet toward approaching traffic
choice_c: 50 feet, 150 feet, and 300 feet behind the vehicle only
explanation: On a one-way or divided highway, place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet toward the approaching traffic.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-11

question: Total stopping distance is the sum of which three distances?
choice_a: Perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance
choice_b: Sight distance, turning distance, and braking distance
choice_c: Following distance, curve distance, and stopping distance
choice_d: Reaction distance, gear distance, and coasting distance
explanation: Total Stopping Distance equals Perception Distance plus Reaction Distance plus Braking Distance.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-12

question: At 55 mph, the average alert driver's perception distance (from seeing a hazard to the brain recognizing it) accounts for about how many feet traveled?
explanation: The average perception time for an alert driver is about 1.75 seconds, which accounts for 142 feet traveled at 55 mph.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-12

question: On a wet road, you should generally reduce your speed by about how much compared to your dry-road speed?
explanation: The manual advises reducing speed by about one-third on a wet road (for example, slowing from 55 to about 35 mph).
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-13

question: On packed snow, how much should you reduce your speed compared to dry-road speed?
choice_c: By about a half or more
explanation: On packed snow, reduce speed by a half, or more; on ice, reduce speed to a crawl and stop driving as soon as it is safe to do so.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-13

topic: Effect of Speed on Stopping Distance
question: When you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, how much greater does the braking distance become?
explanation: Doubling speed from 20 to 40 mph increases the impact and braking distance 4 times; tripling the speed to 60 mph makes it 9 times greater.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-13

question: Hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as:
explanation: It does not take a lot of water to cause hydroplaning; it can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is a lot of water on the road.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-14

question: What is the general rule for following distance at speeds below 40 mph?
choice_a: At least one second for every 10 feet of vehicle length
choice_b: A fixed 2 seconds regardless of vehicle length
choice_c: One car length for every 10 mph
choice_d: Half a second for every 10 feet of vehicle length
explanation: One good rule says you need at least one second for each 10 feet of vehicle length at speeds below 40 mph, adding one more second for speeds above 40 mph.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-15

question: A red triangle with an orange center displayed on a vehicle is the symbol for:
explanation: The slow-moving vehicle symbol, a red triangle with an orange center, warns other drivers that a vehicle such as a moped, farm machinery, or construction equipment is slow by nature.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-19

question: Under federal regulations, how long is a CDL disqualified after a second conviction within three years for hand-held mobile telephone use while driving a CMV?
explanation: A CDL will be disqualified for 60 days for a second offense of hand-held mobile telephone use within 3 years, and 120 days for three or more offenses within 3 years.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-21

question: How long is a CDL disqualified for a second texting-while-driving conviction within three years?
explanation: Just as with hand-held phone use, a CDL will be disqualified 60 days for the second texting offense within 3 years, and 120 days for three or more offenses.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-21

question: How does the manual distinguish 'road rage' from 'aggressive driving'?
choice_a: There is no difference between the two terms
choice_b: Road rage involves intent to do harm or physically assault another driver, while aggressive driving is selfish, bold, or pushy driving without regard for others' safety
choice_c: Aggressive driving is a criminal offense while road rage is not
choice_d: Road rage only applies to passenger vehicles
explanation: Aggressive driving is operating a vehicle in a selfish, bold, or pushy manner without regard for others' rights or safety; road rage is operating a vehicle with the intent to harm others or physically assault a driver or their vehicle.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-22
